# remotty agent guide

## Product

remotty provides an installable PWA for following and controlling local OpenCode sessions remotely: messages, diffs, todos, questions, permission requests, prompts, stop, and agent switching. The local OpenCode plugin makes an outbound connection; OpenCode remains local.

## Hosted install

Requirements: OpenCode and Node.js >=22 for npx.

1. Install the plugin: `opencode plugin opencode-remotty --global --force`.
2. Create an invitation: `npx --yes --package opencode-remotty@latest remotty pair`.
3. The CLI output is human-oriented and contains a sensitive token, fragment-only pairing URL, and QR code. The invite expires after 10 minutes. Agents must not publish, log to public systems, or share this output.
4. Open the printed pairing URL, scan its QR code, or paste the token at https://remotty.devve.space/pair.
5. Quit any running OpenCode process, then run `opencode --continue`.
6. Verify that the PWA shows the local session.

The CLI mutates `~/.config/remotty/config.json`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/remotty/config.json` when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set. It stores relay authority keys, device records, invitation hashes, revocation state, and replay records with mode 0600.

## CLI

Run CLI commands with `npx --yes --package opencode-remotty@latest remotty <command>` so they do not depend on a PATH-installed binary: `npx --yes --package opencode-remotty@latest remotty pair`, `npx --yes --package opencode-remotty@latest remotty invite`, `npx --yes --package opencode-remotty@latest remotty devices`, `npx --yes --package opencode-remotty@latest remotty revoke <device-id>`, `npx --yes --package opencode-remotty@latest remotty remove <device-id>`, `npx --yes --package opencode-remotty@latest remotty remove --revoked`, and `npx --yes --package opencode-remotty@latest remotty status`.

For a custom broker and app, the supported form is: `npx --yes --package opencode-remotty@latest remotty pair --broker wss://broker.example/ws --app https://app.example`. Pairing bundles carry the broker URL; the web build does not need a broker URL environment variable. `REMOTTY_URL`, `REMOTTY_APP_URL`, and `REMOTTY_NAME` are supported environment overrides. Use loopback `ws://` and `http://` only for local development.

## Local development

Repository parity is Node 24 and pnpm 11.6.0. Install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. In one terminal run `pnpm build` and `pnpm dev`. In another, run `REMOTTY_URL=ws://localhost:8787/ws REMOTTY_APP_URL=http://localhost:5173 node packages/plugin/dist/cli.js pair`. Open the printed URL or http://localhost:5173/pair, then quit OpenCode and run `opencode --continue`.

## Security contract

The broker only routes opaque, signed ciphertext. It must not receive plaintext messages, diffs, commands, or notification content. Protocol changes affect `packages/protocol`, `packages/plugin`, `apps/web`, and `apps/broker` together. The broker can observe room/device identifiers, Push endpoints, frame sizes, and timing, and can delay or drop traffic.

## Repository and verification

`packages/plugin` is the publishable CLI/plugin; `packages/protocol` owns validated shared protocol; `apps/broker` owns WebSocket/Push routing; `apps/web` owns the PWA. For cross-package changes run `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, and `git diff --check`. For plugin publish changes run `pnpm --filter opencode-remotty pack --dry-run`. Do not edit generated `dist/`, `dev-dist/`, or `.vite/`; `apps/web/public/notification-sw.js` is authored source.
